title: The Story Behind Ankara Print — and How We Cut It
excerpt: Ankara's bold wax prints carry decades of design history. Cutting a garment from it means respecting that pattern, not just the yardage.
author: Lipek Fashion Team
body: Ankara wax-print fabric has roots that trace through West African textile trade, evolving into a design language of its own — each motif and colourway often carries a name and a meaning within local fashion culture.

Because the prints are large and directional, cutting a garment isn't a simple layout problem. We plan panel placement on the fabric before a single cut is made, so a bold central motif lands on the chest or back panel intentionally, not chopped across a side seam.
This planning stage often takes longer than the sewing itself for multi-panel garments, but it's the difference between a print that looks intentional and one that looks accidental.
We stock a rotating selection of Ankara prints in-atelier, and happily work with fabric clients bring in from their own sourcing trips.
